standard.title: Respect and empathy in relationships
standard.description: describe and demonstrate how respect and empathy can be expressed to positively influence relationships
standard.prior_knowledge: At Years 3-4, students selected, used and refined personal and social skills to establish, manage and strengthen relationships (AC9HP4P04). They have a repertoire of relationship skills. This descriptor requires specifically demonstrating respect and empathy as relationship-influencing mechanisms, and understanding how language and behaviour directed at others (including First Nations Australians) can affect relationships.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe and demonstrate how respect and empathy can be expressed to positively influence relationships in a range of contexts.

nodes.label: Understanding respect and empathy as distinct capacities
nodes.description: Distinguish between respect and empathy as relational capacities — understanding what each means as an active behaviour and how each operates differently in relationships.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the difference between respect and empathy as relationship behaviours, with a concrete example of each.
success_criteria: Can describe both concepts specifically — empathy is not just 'being nice', respect is not just 'being polite'
Examples demonstrate the distinction, not the same behaviour labelled differently
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who conflate respect and empathy (treating them as synonyms for 'being nice') will not be able to deliberately demonstrate either in a focused way, undermining both the 'describe' and 'demonstrate' demands of the descriptor.

response_modes.reason: Contrast the two: when is empathy the right response? when is respect? Scenario-based discussion that surfaces the distinction through cases rather than definition-recitation.

nodes.label: Demonstrating expression of respect and empathy
nodes.description: Practise expressing respect and empathy in a range of relationship contexts — including changing relationships, dealing with conflict and bullying, and building new connections.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least one expression of respect and one of empathy in a role-play or live scenario, and describe the effect on the relationship.
success_criteria: Expression is behavioural — something visible and specific, not just an internal feeling
Can describe the effect on the relationship, not just report that the expression was made
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Respect and empathy are expressed differently across diverse relationship contexts: changing relationships (new school, team change), cross-cultural relationships (including relationships with First Nations Australians and the role of language), bullying and harassment situations, and new friendships.

response_modes.reason: Practise expressions of respect and empathy across contexts: relationship changes; dealing with bullying; building cross-cultural connections including awareness of language that can cause offence to First Nations Australians. Each context demands different relational behaviour.

nodes.label: Connecting expressions to relationship outcomes
nodes.description: Analyse how deliberate expressions of respect and empathy influence the quality and direction of relationships — making the connection from behaviour to relationship outcome explicit.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe a situation in which expressing respect or empathy changed or positively influenced a relationship, and explain the connection between the expression and the outcome.
success_criteria: Relationship outcome is described specifically (not just 'things got better')
The connection between the expression and the outcome is explained, not asserted

response_modes.reason: Connects the description and demonstration of respect and empathy to their relationship-influencing effect — the full descriptor demand of 'positively influence relationships'.
